title_tag: 10 Best Hotels in Downtown Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Downtown Dubai hotels from €95 to €459 a night near Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall: fountain views, walk times, metro, pools and breakfast compared.
h1_main: 10 Best Hotels in Downtown Dubai in 2026
author_role: 10 Downtown hotels compared on price, guest score, walk to Dubai Mall, metro, pools and room size
price_note: Lowest nightly rate for 2 adults on 13–14 January 2027. Dates, room type and board change it; taxes and the Dubai tourism fee are added at booking.
lead: For most couples the best hotel in Downtown Dubai is Kempinski The Boulevard at €459 a night: the top guest score of the 10 (9.4), a balcony in every room and two pools, a short walk from Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. Want the fountain from your window? Palace Downtown sells Fountain View rooms from €576. On a budget, Hotel Boulevard scores 9.3 for €222, and families get a 75 m² suite with a kitchen at Wyndham for €139.

All 10 are compared below on the nightly price for the same date, guest score, location score, walk to Dubai Mall and the metro, pools, breakfast and room size. Use the filters for 5-star icons, suites with kitchens, families, rooms under €250 or metro access, or jump to the comparison table.

items.title: Kempinski The Boulevard Dubai

pills.label: In 15:00 · out 12:00
pills.body: From 15:00, check-out until 12:00. Photo ID and a credit card are needed at check-in, and the hotel asks you to tell it your arrival time in advance.

pills.body: The €459 Deluxe King (or twin) is 506 ft², about 47 m², with a balcony and a bath. The Grand Premier Burj View twin is 581 ft² (54 m²) from €546.

pills.body: Chandeliered lobby and a French brasserie, on the Boulevard close to Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. Pick it for couples who want the highest score in Downtown.

items.skip: if you want to look straight at the fountain from bed: Palace Downtown (#3) and Address Dubai Mall (#5) sell fountain-view rooms.

review: Kempinski The Boulevard has the highest guest score of any hotel in this comparison, 9.4, and its sub-scores are just as strong: 9.7 for location, 9.6 for comfort and staff, 9.5 for cleanliness. It sits on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard, close to Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall.

For €459 a night the entry room is a 47 m² Deluxe King or twin with a balcony and a bath, and the cheapest rate shows free cancellation with no prepayment. If you want the tower in the frame, the Grand Premier Burj View twin is 54 m² from €546. You also get two outdoor pools (one on the roof), a spa with sauna and steam room, and a French brasserie.

Compared with Palace Downtown (#3, €436) you pay €23 more for a higher score and a French brasserie and balcony rooms instead of Arabian décor and a fountain view. Compared with Hotel Boulevard (#2, €222) you pay about double for a bigger room, a second pool and a spa.
Catches: taxes come on top of the €459 (5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night), the spa is paid, and children from 13 are charged as adults.

items.title: Hotel Boulevard, Autograph Collection, Downtown Dubai

pills.label: In 15:00–00:00 · out 12:00
pills.body: Check-in runs from 15:00 to midnight, check-out until 12:00. Photo ID and a credit card are needed, and the hotel wants your arrival time in advance.

pills.label: 32 m² Deluxe
pills.body: The €222 Deluxe King or Twin is 344 ft², about 32 m², with a minibar. Every room at the hotel has a balcony with city or pool views.

pills.label: No cots or extra beds
pills.body: Children of any age are welcome, but from 12 they pay as adults and the hotel has no cots or extra beds. Best for couples or two friends.

pills.label: Breakfast €31
pills.body: Breakfast costs €31 on the cheapest rate; breakfast-included rates start at €249 a night.

pills.label: Outdoor pool
pills.body: An outdoor pool with sun terrace and loungers, plus a fitness room. There is no spa here.

pills.label: Pets allowed
pills.body: The only hotel of the 10 that accepts pets (charges may apply). Bicycle rental is offered too.

pills.label: Boutique, arty
pills.body: A smaller 4★ in the Old Town part of the Boulevard, every room with a balcony. Two restaurants: Canvas (Middle Eastern) and Collage (international).

items.pick: for couples who want a 9.3-rated hotel with a 9.7 location score for €222, about half the price of the Boulevard 5-stars.
items.skip: if you travel with a baby or a third person: there are no cots or extra beds.

review: Hotel Boulevard is the reason this page does not tell you to spend €450. It scores 9.3 overall and 9.7 for location, the same location score as Kempinski, for €222 a night. Its value-for-money score, 9.2, is the highest in the comparison.

You get a 32 m² Deluxe room with a balcony over the city or the pool, an outdoor pool, a fitness room and two restaurants. What you give up against the 5-stars: no spa, one pool and smaller rooms. Breakfast is €31 extra on the cheapest rate, or pick a breakfast rate from €249.

Read the rate rules. The €222 price is non-refundable and charged before arrival; the free-cancellation, pay-at-the-hotel rate is €247. Taxes come on top: 5% VAT, 7% municipality fee and an AED 15 tourism fee a night (the 5-stars charge AED 20).

Against its Downtown neighbour at this price, Wyndham (#4, €139), you trade Wyndham's 75 m² suite and kitchen for a higher score and a boutique feel. It is also the only hotel of the 10 that allows pets.

items.title: Palace Downtown

pills.label: Fountain on the doorstep
pills.body: The hotel overlooks the Dubai Fountain and the lake around Burj Khalifa, a 5-minute walk from Dubai Mall and Souk Al Bahar.

pills.label: Hammam spa
pills.body: Arabian-style spa with hammam, monsoon showers, hot tub and steam rooms, plus a gym with a personal trainer.

pills.label: 6 restaurants
pills.body: Six venues, from Thiptara (Thai, romantic) to Ewaan (Middle Eastern buffet, breakfast to dinner) and high tea at Al Bayt.

pills.label: Arabian palace
pills.body: Built as a traditional Arabian palace, with a palm-fringed pool and Arabian décor in every room, overlooking the fountain and Burj Lake.

items.pick: for a special-occasion stay where the Dubai Fountain is the view: book the Fountain View room (from €576) and you watch the shows from your room.
items.skip: if value matters: its 8.4 value score is among the lowest here, and the cheapest €436 room faces the lake, not the fountain.

review: If the picture in your head is the Dubai Fountain from your balcony, this is the hotel. Palace Downtown overlooks the fountain and the lake around Burj Khalifa, and it is a 5-minute walk to Dubai Mall and Souk Al Bahar. Its location score is 9.6.

Know which room you are buying. The €436 Deluxe is a Lake View room. The Fountain View Deluxe (51 m²) starts at €576, and a 70 m² Junior Suite with a balcony over the lake is €579, which is the better deal if the fountain is not essential.

The hotel is built like a low Arabian palace, with a palm-fringed pool, a spa with hammam and monsoon showers, and six restaurants. That setting is what you pay for: its overall score (8.8) and value score (8.4) trail Kempinski (#1) and Hotel Boulevard (#2).

Catches: there are no extra beds (cots are free for under-4s), and taxes and the tourism fee are added at booking. For the view from the top instead, see our Burj Khalifa ticket comparison; the tower is next door.

review: Wyndham is the best deal in Downtown for anyone who needs space. The €139 rate is not a standard room: it is a 75 m² one-bedroom suite with a balcony over the Boulevard, a full kitchen with dishwasher, and a hot tub. The hotel has 181 suites, all with kitchens and laundry.

It sits next to Dubai Opera, overlooking Burj Khalifa and the fountain, a 10-minute walk to Dubai Mall. The free shuttle covers Dubai Mall, the metro and Jumeirah Beach Park, which saves taxi money if you want a beach day.

For kids it has a kids' pool, indoor and outdoor play areas, interconnecting suites and free cots for under-3s. With 8,993 reviews it is also the most-reviewed hotel in the comparison and still scores 9.0, with 9.6 for location.

Catches: an AED 300 cash deposit on arrival (cards only for payment), one restaurant, and taxes on top (5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night). Breakfast is not in the €139 rate; that rate gives 25% off food and drink, and breakfast rates start at €231.

review: Address Dubai Mall's selling point is in one line of its description: it connects directly into Dubai Mall through a link bridge. You shop and eat without stepping outside or crossing a road, and you can drop bags in your room halfway through.

The €412 room is a 50 m² Deluxe on a high floor facing the city skyline. The Burj Khalifa and Fountain View room with a balcony is the next category up, and Club rooms add a lounge that serves lunch, afternoon tea and dinner, which can pay for itself if you would eat there anyway.

Families get three pools (one for kids), a children's playroom and free cots for under-4s. The trade-off is value: guests score it 8.3 for value for money, the lowest of the 10, and Kempinski (#1) is €47 more for a 9.4 hotel on the same Boulevard.
Taxes and the tourism fee are added at booking.

review: Address Sky View is the hotel for the infinity pool on level 54, high above the Downtown skyline. The €456 Premier Room includes access to it, and at 678 ft² (63 m²) it is the largest entry room of the hotel-style 5-stars here that list a size; only the suites at #4 and #7 are bigger.

Evenings are covered in-house: six restaurants and bars, including CÉ LA VI for Asian food and cocktails and Amelia for Japanese-Peruvian. If your evening is a rooftop drink rather than a fountain show, you do not need to leave the building.

Against Kempinski (#1, €459) it costs the same, scores slightly lower (9.1 vs 9.4) and puts the emphasis on its rooftop pool and bars. Against Address Dubai Mall (#5) you get bigger rooms and a better score, but no bridge into the mall.

Catches: breakfast is €41 unless your rate includes it, taxes come on top (5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night), and there are no extra beds. Free cancellation is offered on some rates up to 6 January for this stay.

review: DAMAC Maison Mall Street is the cheapest way to sleep on the Boulevard itself. For €137 you get a 70 m² City View Deluxe with a kitchenette and a balcony over the pool and the city, and the rate shows free cancellation with nothing to pay until you arrive. Its location score, 9.7, ties the best in this comparison.

It runs as serviced apartments: every unit has a balcony facing Burj Khalifa, the city or the Dubai Fountain, a dining area and a kitchen. For a family, the two-bedroom unit (130 m²) shows €344 for this date, less than a single room at Palace Downtown; add your children's ages when you search to see the exact price.
Against Wyndham (#4, €139), the other big-space option, it sits on the Boulevard itself and is €2 cheaper, while Wyndham adds a free shuttle and more for kids. Both score 9.0.
Catches: a AED 1,000 deposit on your credit card, check-in only until 23:30 (tell them if you land late), and taxes and the tourism fee on top.

review: The Dubai EDITION is the pick if dinner and drinks are the point of the trip. It has five restaurants in one building, Italian at Duomo, Japanese at Ken by Kamatsuda, Indian at Masti, cocktails at Hush by Blackstar and brunch at Thia Skylounge, plus live music and a rooftop pool.
For €324 the Guest King is a 42 m² soundproofed room with a balcony and city view. Location scores 9.7, joint best in this comparison.

It sits between the two price groups: about €130 under Kempinski (#1) and Address Sky View (#6), about €100 over Hotel Boulevard (#2). You pay that premium for the design and the dining, not for space.

review: If you plan to use the metro, Sofitel solves it. The hotel is on Sheikh Zayed Road beside Burj Khalifa metro station, while Dubai Mall is a short walk and Burj Khalifa about 10 minutes.

For €244 you get a 5-star Luxury King with walk-in shower and bath, a 5th-floor pool terrace with a bar, and a spa with sauna. Breakfast is €25, the cheapest hotel breakfast in this comparison, and every room is listed as wheelchair accessible.

The trade-off is the setting. You are on Sheikh Zayed Road, not on the Boulevard, and the location score (9.3) is below the 9.6–9.7 of the Boulevard hotels. Hotel Boulevard (#2) costs €22 less and scores higher, but has no metro next door.
Catches: the €244 rate is not refundable as shown (free-cancellation rates from €284), and taxes come on top (5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night).

guide.h2: Downtown Dubai Hotels Compared: Price, Score and Walk to Dubai Mall
guide.html:
Every price is the lowest nightly rate for 2 adults on the same January night, before taxes. Six of them (Kempinski, Palace Downtown, Address Dubai Mall, Address Sky View, DAMAC and Leva) were limited-time deal rates that night, so expect those to rise when the deal ends. The pattern is clear: the Boulevard 5-stars cluster at €412–459, while three hotels with location scores of 9.6–9.7 cost €222 or less.

What the numbers say: per square metre, the suite hotels win by a mile. Wyndham's 75 m² suite works out at about €1.85 per m² a night and DAMAC Maison Mall Street's 70 m² at about €1.96, against roughly €9.80 at Kempinski and €8.20 at Address Dubai Mall. You pay the 5-star premium for service, pools and views, not space.

guide.h2: Which Downtown Dubai Hotel Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Couples, one or two nights, want the best: Kempinski The Boulevard (€459, 9.4).
  • The Dubai Fountain from your room: Palace Downtown, but book the Fountain View Deluxe (from €576), not the €436 Lake View.
  • Best score for the money: Hotel Boulevard (€222, 9.3, value 9.2). Book the €247 rate if you need free cancellation.
  • Families or 4+ nights: Wyndham (€139 for a 75 m² suite, kids' pool, free mall and beach shuttle) or DAMAC Maison Mall Street (€137, 2-bedroom units from €344).
  • Shopping trip: Address Dubai Mall, linked to the mall by a bridge.
  • Infinity-pool photo and rooftop bars: Address Sky View.
  • Restaurants and nightlife under one roof: The Dubai EDITION (€324).
  • Using the metro a lot: Sofitel (beside Burj Khalifa station, €244) or Leva (€95, 5 minutes' walk).

If you are choosing between areas rather than hotels, compare Dubai Marina hotels for the waterfront, Palm Jumeirah hotels for a beach, or Dubai's best luxury hotels across the city. Downtown has no beach of its own; Wyndham's free shuttle to Jumeirah Beach Park is the easiest fix.

guide.h2: Staying in Downtown Dubai: Where, Getting Around and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Which part of Downtown

Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard loops around Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall. Kempinski, Address Sky View, DAMAC Maison Mall Street and Hotel Boulevard (in the Old Town section) are on it. Palace Downtown and Address Dubai Mall sit closest to the fountain and the mall. Wyndham is at the Dubai Opera end, a 10-minute walk from the mall. Sofitel and Leva are on Sheikh Zayed Road, the metro side: closer to trains, further from the fountain. Leva is across the road, with an Al Wasl / City Walk address.

Getting around

Dubai Mall/Burj Khalifa metro station is beside Sofitel and 5 minutes' walk from Leva; Business Bay station is 7 minutes from Leva. Wyndham runs a free shuttle to the metro, Dubai Mall and Jumeirah Beach Park. Dubai International Airport is listed 13–15 km from these hotels, 15–20 minutes by car. Most hotels here include free parking.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: the prices above exclude 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee of AED 20 per room per night at the 5-stars here (AED 15 at Hotel Boulevard).
  • Breakfast: €25 (Sofitel), €30 (EDITION), €31 (Hotel Boulevard), €41 (Address Sky View) on room-only rates.
  • Deposits: AED 1,000 on a credit card at DAMAC Maison Mall Street, AED 300 in cash at Wyndham.
  • Extra beds: AED 150–350 a night where offered; Hotel Boulevard, Palace and Address Sky View have none.

Best months

The prices here are for mid-January, the cool, high season when evenings by the fountain are pleasant. Downtown is also the base for most sightseeing: the tower is next door (see our Burj Khalifa tickets comparison), and many Dubai city tours and desert safaris pick up from Downtown hotels.

faqs.q: What is the best hotel in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.a: Kempinski The Boulevard has the highest guest score of the 10 (9.4) and a 9.7 location score, from €459 a night with a balcony room and two pools. For a lower budget, Hotel Boulevard scores 9.3 for €222.

faqs.q: Which Downtown Dubai hotel has the best Burj Khalifa and fountain views?
faqs.a: Palace Downtown overlooks the Dubai Fountain and Burj Lake; its Fountain View rooms start at €576. Address Dubai Mall sells Burj Khalifa and Fountain View rooms with balconies, and Address Sky View has a level 54 infinity pool facing the tower. Always book the view category: the cheapest room usually faces the lake or the city.

faqs.q: Which hotels are connected to Dubai Mall?
faqs.a: Address Dubai Mall connects directly into Dubai Mall by a link bridge. Palace Downtown is a 5-minute walk, Wyndham 10 minutes (or its free shuttle), and Leva 1 km across Sheikh Zayed Road.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest good hotel near Burj Khalifa?
faqs.a: Leva Hotel and Suites at €95, rated 9.0, 1 km from Burj Khalifa and 5 minutes' walk from the metro, though it is across Sheikh Zayed Road rather than in Downtown. Inside Downtown, DAMAC Maison Mall Street (€137, 70 m²) and Wyndham (€139, 75 m² suite) are the cheapest.

faqs.q: Which Downtown Dubai hotel is best for families?
faqs.a: Wyndham Downtown: one-bedroom suites with kitchens from €139, a kids' pool, indoor and outdoor play areas, free cots and a free shuttle to Dubai Mall and Jumeirah Beach Park. DAMAC Maison Mall Street has 2- and 3-bedroom units and a kids' pool.

faqs.q: Is the tourism fee included in Downtown Dubai hotel prices?
faqs.a: No. The nightly prices on this page exclude 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee (AED 20 per night at the 5-stars here, AED 15 at Hotel Boulevard). They are added at booking.

faqs.q: Is Downtown or Business Bay better for a first trip?
faqs.a: Downtown if you want to walk to Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall and the fountain shows. Business Bay is next door and often cheaper; see our Business Bay hotel comparison. For an evening on the water from either area, compare Dubai dinner cruises.

methodology: We compared 10 hotels in and next to Downtown Dubai side by side on the lowest nightly rate for 2 adults on the same mid-January night, guest score and location score, walking distance to Dubai Mall and the metro, pools, breakfast price, cheapest room size, deposits and child policies. Prices are live rates in euros before taxes and fees. Price per square metre divides that rate by the cheapest room's listed size. We left out hotels that sit in Business Bay or more than 1.5 km from the fountain, and private apartment listings with few reviews.
